newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam jails supreme court judge in graft case.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam jails supreme court judge in graft case.

text.p: Vietnam, seeking to enforce an official crackdown on corruption, said on Monday it had jailed a Supreme Court judge on charges of influence peddling.

Bui Van Tham was found guilty on Saturday of attempting to influence the outcome of a case after accepting $500 in cash and a quantity of gold. A 36-month suspended sentence was given to the woman who gave the bribe, a court official said by phone.

The official was unable to provide details but state-controlled media said a tape-recorded conversation in which Tham admitted offering "beer money" to a third party had been used in the evidence against him in court.
The state prosecutor had originally called for a suspended term against Tham and six to eight years in prison for the woman co-defendant.
But the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper said the final sentence carried a message of deterrence.

"The two-year imprisonment is not only a lesson for Tham but also a warning to anyone who wants to take advantage of the position and power assigned to them by the State and people to make personal profit," it said.

According to independent analysts, Vietnam ranks as one of the most graft-ridden countries in Asia. In recent months, however, the communist government has moved to tackle the problem with a series of high profile sackings and trials.

In early February four people were sentenced to death and a number of others jailed for involvement in a major corruption scandal associated with Ho Chi Minh City firm Tamexco, a Communist Party-affiliated trading firm.
Fifteen people have appealed against the ruling, while state dailies have called for further investigation into the murky details.
